subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: For an object in complete equilibrium under several forces:
options: The resultant force is zero and the resultant moment is zero
The forces must all be equal
questions.explain: Equilibrium requires both zero resultant force and zero resultant moment.

questions.q: A spring of constant 50 N m⁻¹ is extended by 0.20 m. The elastic strain energy stored is:
In SHM, the acceleration is always directed:
questions.explain: The restoring acceleration always points back toward the equilibrium position.

questions.q: For a projectile launched on level ground, which launch angle gives the maximum range (no air resistance)?
questions.explain: Maximum horizontal range occurs at a launch angle of 45° on level ground.

questions.q: According to Newton's third law, action and reaction forces:
options: Are the same type only by coincidence
Are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction on different bodies
questions.explain: Third-law pairs are equal, opposite, of the same type, and act on two different bodies.

questions.q: Tensile strain is defined as:
questions.explain: Strain ε = extension ÷ original length and is a dimensionless ratio.

questions.q: Plastic deformation is characterised by:
options: A permanent change in shape after the load is removed
questions.explain: Plastic deformation leaves a permanent extension once the load is removed.

questions.q: An object moves in a circle of radius r at constant speed v. Its centripetal acceleration is given by:
questions.explain: Centripetal acceleration is a = v²/r, directed toward the centre.

questions.q: In SHM, the phase difference between displacement and acceleration is:
questions.explain: Acceleration is exactly out of phase (π rad) with displacement, since a = −ω²x.

questions.q: A wire under a stress of 1.5 × 10⁸ Pa has a strain of 7.5 × 10⁻⁴. Its Young modulus is:
At the point of maximum displacement in SHM, the oscillator has:
questions.explain: At the extremes velocity is zero and acceleration (restoring force) is maximum.

questions.q: The elastic limit of a material is the point beyond which:
options: The material no longer returns to its original length when unloaded
questions.explain: Beyond the elastic limit, deformation becomes permanent (plastic).

questions.q: The work done by a constant force is given by:
questions.explain: Work equals force times displacement in the direction of the force, W = Fs cosθ.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: Displacement has both magnitude and direction, whereas speed, distance and mass are scalars.

questions.q: Elastic deformation means that when the load is removed, the material:
questions.explain: Elastic deformation is fully recoverable: the material returns to its original shape.

questions.q: For a simple pendulum of length L, the period of small oscillations is:
questions.explain: The simple pendulum period is T = 2π√(L/g).

questions.q: Newton's first law states that a body remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless:
options: A resultant force acts on it
questions.explain: A body's motion only changes when acted on by a non-zero resultant (net) force.

questions.q: A 1000 kg car at 20 m s⁻¹ collides and sticks to a stationary 1000 kg car. Their common velocity afterwards is:
questions.explain: By momentum conservation, 1000×20 = 2000×v, so v = 10 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A 0.50 kg ball moving at 4.0 m s⁻¹ rebounds at 4.0 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction. The magnitude of the change in momentum is:
Why does a crumple zone reduce the force on car occupants in a crash?
options: It increases the time over which momentum changes
It increases the change in momentum
It increases the mass of the car
questions.explain: A longer contact time reduces the rate of change of momentum and hence the force (F = Δp/Δt).

questions.q: A wire of cross-sectional area 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m² carries a tension of 40 N. The tensile stress is:
On a stress–strain graph, a material that absorbs a large amount of energy (large area under the curve) before fracture is described as:
questions.explain: A large area under the stress–strain curve means much energy absorbed before fracture, i.e. the material is tough.

questions.q: A projectile is launched and lands at the same height. At the highest point of its path, its vertical velocity is:
questions.explain: At the peak the vertical component of velocity is momentarily zero.

questions.q: A ductile material is one that:
options: Does not obey Hooke's law at all
Can undergo large plastic deformation and be drawn into wires
questions.explain: Ductile materials (e.g. copper) deform plastically a great deal and can be drawn into wires.

questions.q: A spring extends 0.040 m when a force of 8.0 N is applied. Its spring constant is:
Density is defined as:
questions.explain: Density ρ = mass ÷ volume, with units kg m⁻³.

questions.q: In SHM, the phase difference between displacement and velocity is:
questions.explain: Velocity leads displacement by π/2 (a quarter cycle) in SHM.

questions.q: A brittle material is one that:
options: Undergoes large plastic deformation before breaking
Breaks suddenly with little or no plastic deformation
questions.explain: Brittle materials (e.g. glass) fracture abruptly with negligible plastic deformation.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph for a spring obeying Hooke's law, the gradient equals:
questions.explain: The gradient of a force–extension graph is the spring constant k.

questions.q: Tensile stress is defined as:
questions.explain: Stress σ = force ÷ cross-sectional area, with units Pa (N m⁻²).
